clue.text: Detailing its role in the nursery rhyme

definitions.text: Detailing its role in the nursery rhyme

parts.words: Detailing its role in the nursery rhyme
parts.note: read 'detailing' as de-tailing: the tool that cut off the tails of the three blind mice in the rhyme

explanation.surface: Someone describing the part a household object plays in a children's verse.
explanation.walkthrough: In the rhyme Three Blind Mice, the farmer's wife cuts off their tails; 'Detailing' means removing tails, not giving details.
explanation.definitionFit: The farmer's wife in Three Blind Mice uses this kitchen blade to dock the mice's tails.

clue.text: Garage open all night

parts.note: not a filling station that never closes but a shelter for a vehicle that has no doors, so it is always open

explanation.surface: A petrol station that trades round the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garage open all night' suggests a 24-hour service station; it means a roofed parking space with open sides.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a roof over a parking space with open sides, a garage that can never be shut.

clue.text: Ways out of the Russian capital for special planes

indicators.note: the ways stand outside, so the first word holds the other letter within it

parts.note: ways or courses are routes

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first, upper-case letter

explanation.surface: Escape routes from Moscow laid on for particular aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian capital' tempts you toward Moscow, but it is just the letter R. 'Planes' are carpentry tools, not aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A router is a woodworker's plane for cutting grooves, so these are specialised planing tools.

clue.text: Insect working well in the grass

parts.note: someone working well is in form
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug thriving down in the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like the lawn the insect lives in, but it is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a grass is someone who tells tales to the police, an informer.

clue.text: Belly-band needs loosening to be right

indicators.note: loosening the letters of the word right lets them fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A strap round a horse's middle must be slackened before it sits properly.
explanation.definitionFit: A girth is the strap passing under a horse's belly to hold the saddle on.

clue.text: Paul Revere's feat reported in the compound

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the phrase

parts.note: Paul Revere made a famous night ride in 1775 to warn of British troops

explanation.surface: An American patriot's famous exploit described within a fortified enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' seems an enclosure, but it is a chemical compound.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitride is a chemical compound of nitrogen with another element.

clue.text: Ties where restraint is called for

explanation.surface: Neckwear appropriate to occasions demanding self-control.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetters are chains or shackles that tie someone up, and such restraints are what a prisoner needing restraint is put in.

clue.text: Wearing glasses for a show when retired

indicators.note: the show happens when one has retired, that is within bed

parts.note: someone who has retired for the night is in bed
a spectacle is a show

explanation.surface: Putting on one's specs to watch a performance after leaving work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' suggests leaving work; it means gone to bed, and the show sits inside BED.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles are glasses, so someone who has them on is bespectacled.

clue.text: Listener needs this protection from bungler on the organ

indicators.note: in a down light one part sits on another, here the bungler written after the organ

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing
a muff is a clumsy person who fumbles

explanation.surface: A listener needs shielding from a clumsy musician at the church keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the instrument, but it is the body part that hears.
explanation.definitionFit: Earmuffs are padded covers that guard the ears against cold or noise.

clue.text: Call again about the ownership

parts.note: re means about, concerning
title is legal ownership of property

explanation.surface: Phoning back on the subject of who owns something.
explanation.definitionFit: To retitle is to name something afresh, giving it a new name.

clue.text: Flower girl in finale appears briefly in South Pacific

indicators.note: the flower and the girl are placed inside the word for finale

parts.note: the finale is the end
an aster is a garden flower
Isla is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A flower girl makes a brief appearance at the close of the musical South Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears briefly' only links the wordplay to the definition. 'South Pacific' looks like the musical but is the ocean where the island lies.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chilean island, famous for its giant stone heads, lies in the south-eastern Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Holy king retains ace explorer

indicators.note: the holy king keeps the ace within, holding it inside

parts.note: pi is short for pious, holy
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword royal abbreviation used here for a monarch
an ace counts as one

explanation.surface: A saintly monarch keeps a top adventurer at court.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is one of the first to explore or settle new territory.

clue.text: She succeeded as Catherine Sloper

explanation.surface: An actress triumphed in the role of a Henry James character.
explanation.walkthrough: Catherine Sloper is the rich young woman of Henry James's Washington Square, staged and filmed as The Heiress.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who succeeds to a fortune inherits it; Catherine Sloper is the wealthy title character of the play and film adapted from James.

clue.text: Places in speech for quotes

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken, so the word sounds like the one for places

parts.note: places are sites

explanation.surface: Spots in a talk where someone uses quotations.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite something is to quote it as an authority.

clue.text: In a river without a costume? One will get a letter!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the river lies around the costume

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a costume is a dress

explanation.surface: Swimming in a river with no swimsuit on? Someone's sure to write in about it!
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old sense 'outside', so the river wraps round the costume. The Dee is a British river.
explanation.definitionFit: The addressee is the person to whom mail is sent.

clue.text: In natural religion, recognise absolute rule

indicators.note: the spotting goes in the religion, inside it

parts.note: deism is belief in God based on reason and nature rather than revelation
to spot is to recognise

explanation.surface: Within a faith based on nature, one sees tyranny.
explanation.definitionFit: Despotism is government by a tyrant with unlimited power.

clue.text: Device to blow up a satrap

indicators.note: blow means scatter, as letters are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A machine for detonating a Persian provincial governor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow up' reads as one verb, but 'blow' alone is the anagram signal and 'up' joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus is equipment or a mechanism designed for a task.

clue.text: A canape is enough to make you feel good

definitions.text: A canape is enough to make you feel good

indicators.note: to make here is to form the letters of the earlier words into something new

explanation.surface: A single nibble at a party can cheer you up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' rearranges the letters of 'canape' into PANACE, and the clue's opening A goes on the end; the whole clue then describes a cure-all.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a remedy for every ill, something guaranteed to restore wellbeing.

clue.text: Made off with bag for loot

parts.note: made off means ran away
a sack is a bag

explanation.surface: A thief fled with a holdall full of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack is to plunder or pillage a place.

clue.text: Very musical

parts.note: a direction in a score meaning 'very', as in allegro of this kind

explanation.definitionFit: In music this Italian word modifies a tempo marking to mean extremely, as in allegro assai.

clue.text: Run in a race and pretend to win

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, is a motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
to act is to pretend

explanation.surface: Taking part in a race and faking a victory.
explanation.definitionFit: To win people over, as in winning admirers, is to attract them.

clue.text: An egg that's run looks more, sickly

definitions.text: An egg that's run looks more, sickly

parts.words: An egg that's run looks more, sickly
parts.note: a runny egg on the plate looks more unwell and unappetising

explanation.definitionFit: Seedy means unwell or shabby, so seedier is in a worse state of health.

clue.text: Materials used in the interior of brakes

definitions.text: Materials used in the interior of brakes

parts.words: Materials used in the interior of brakes
parts.note: the friction material inside a vehicle's brake drums, or a garment's inner fabric

explanation.definitionFit: Linings are inner layers of material, such as fabric in a coat or friction pads in brakes.

clue.text: Nokomis, upset, forsakes Oklahoma for a penniless lad

indicators.note: forsakes means abandons, so those letters are dropped
upset in a down light means turned upside down, so the name reads backwards

parts.note: OK is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Oklahoma

explanation.surface: Hiawatha's grandmother, distressed, leaves a US state for a poor boy.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversing NOKOMIS gives SIMOKON; removing OK leaves the answer. Simple Simon in the nursery rhyme had no penny for the pieman.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple Simon of the nursery rhyme could not pay the pieman because he had not a penny.

clue.text: Porridge-maker has nothing at breakfast, say

parts.note: O is the zero figure, nothing
breakfast is an example of a meal

explanation.surface: Someone who cooks porridge eats nothing in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal is ground oats, the ingredient porridge is made from.

clue.text: Harangue Alice wrongly dividing foreign currency

indicators.note: the anagram splits the currency in two, sitting inside it

parts.note: DM is the Deutschmark, former German currency

indicators.note: wrongly means these letters are set out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A woman is wrongly lectured while splitting up some euros.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' gives ECLAI from the name, and 'dividing' sets it inside the old German Deutschmark abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim is to speak rhetorically and vehemently, as in a harangue.

clue.text: Language derived from a Latin one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: derived from means made out of these letters reworked

explanation.surface: A tongue that grew out of Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'derived from' rearranges the letters of 'a Latin' into TALIAN; the Roman numeral for 'one' starts the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian is a Romance tongue spoken in Italy.

clue.text: It is not to be fed during one's stay

definitions.text: It is not to be fed during one's stay

parts.words: It is not to be fed during one's stay
parts.note: a roadside coin box that should not be topped up to extend a parking stay beyond the limit

explanation.definitionFit: A coin-operated device on a street, it times how long a car may stay in a bay.
